messages:
deploy-bot: Started canary rollout of embeddings-service v2.14.3 -> 5% traffic. commit=9a7f3b. change-window=2026-03-09T18:00Z-20:00Z. watch: slo/embeddings-error-rate
Alex: noted, watching SLOs :eyes:
Maya: grafana spike visible on error-rate panel, 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> 3.8% in last 6m https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/embeddings/slo?var-window=30m
Riley: seeing connection pool exhaustion logs from the embedding workers, a few 504s in canary pods
Riley: logs snippet:
```
ERROR embeddings::handler request_id=fd23 status=504 reason="pg timeout" upstream=pg-embeddings pool_wait=128ms
```
Katie: is this new DB query shape from 9a7f3b? commit message mentioned a join for metadata enrichment
Alex: looks like the enrichment increased average request DB time x3 under rate. error budget burn = ~12% of 30d in last 6m (projection) :warning:
Maya: suggestion: pause rollout and pin traffic back to v2.14.2 for embeddings route until we confirm DB optimization or fallback behavior
Katie: agree. can we do a partial rollback for route=embeddings only? we shouldn't rollback the whole service fleet right now
Riley: we have a route-level traffic pin command. running:
```
redwoodctl rollout pin --service embeddings-service --version v2.14.2 --window 10m
```
sre-runbook-bot: Command accepted. initiating traffic pin, will shift 100% of canary traffic to v2.14.2 over 30s and hold.
Riley: pin completed, canary pods now receiving v2.14.2. monitoring…
Alex: error-rate back down to baseline in the last 2m. latency also trending down :thumbsup:
Maya: great. please add a short blurb to the release notes about the enrichment change + DB impact and mark v2.14.3 as blocked for embeddings until a fix
Katie: I'll open a PR for a targeted fix and add an integration test to catch the heavy join path
Riley: runbook note: add test to canary checklist to measure DB p95 on enriched path. tagging oncall for post-mortem if needed
Alex: thanks all. we've paused the rollout, pin stays for 30m window. if green we can reattempt with DB pool tweak or query optimization. :white_check_mark:
